highlights:
## Egypt (FIFA ranking – 29)
[...]
The Pharoahs are back in the World Cup for the first time since 2018 and have a golden opportunity to make its first knockout stage. In addition to Egypt’s greatest player Mohamed Salah, the roster features his successor in Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush. Those two led Egypt to the semifinals of last year’s Africa Cup of Nations and will look to lead Egypt to the knockout stage.
[...]
## France (FIFA ranking – 3)
[...]
Schedule: Senegal (June 16), Iraq (June 22), Norway (June 26)
[...]
The 2018 champions and 2022 runners-up are loaded to make a run at a third straight World Cup final appearance. France arguably has the best roster at this World Cup, particularly in attack with Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, and Michael Olise leading the line. This tournament will also be the last go for manager Didier Deschamps, who looks to lead Les Bleus to a third World Cup title.
[...]
## Senegal (FIFA ranking – 15)
[...]
Schedule: France (June 16), Norway (June 22), Iraq (June 26)
[...]
The Lions of Tarenga come into North America as the “champions” of Africa after a controversial stripping of their AFCON title to Morocco. Regardless, the team brings back stars Sadio Mane, Edouard Mendy, and Kalidou Koulibaly. In any other group, Senegal would be seen as a definitive top-two team but with France and Norway in the way, it will be a gauntlet to avoid a third-place spot.

## Norway (FIFA ranking – 31)
[...]
Schedule: Iraq (June 16), Senegal (June 22), France (June 26)
[...]
Sometimes a generational player can put a nation into the World Cup. That is what happened with Norway as Manchester City striker Erling Haaland led his nation to its first World Cup since 1998. Haaland scored a ridiculous 16 goals in eight qualifying games and with other talent surrounding him, like Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard, this team is capable of a deep run.

Group I is arguably the toughest at the tournament. The final group game could feature a mouth-watering striker battle between Haaland and France’s Kylian Mbappe, with the winner of the Haaland versus Mbappe debate potentially providing the defining subplot of the tournament if both sides have already qualified.
[...]
If Norway’s limitations are exposed, it will be against a truly elite team in the knockout rounds. The overreliance on Haaland and Ødegaard is a genuine vulnerability, and there are questions over whether the defence will stand up to the most elite attacks in the competition. But for a team that qualified with a perfect record, scored 37 goals in eight games and have a striker who scored 16 times in qualifying alone, anything less than progressing from the group would be seen as a major disappointment in Norway. With Haaland up front, the dark horse label has never been more apt.

## Story

Norway 2026 World Cup Preview: Predictions, Betting Odds - Bytes Europe

Close Menu

Share

Find a full preview for Norway ahead of the 2026 World Cup, including betting odds, key players, predictions and more.

Norway enters the 2026 World Cup as arguably the most intriguing team in the entire tournament, with unbelievable offensive potential but a relatively unproven squad on the international stage. Here’s a full preview of the Norwegian national team, including predictions, betting odds, key players and more.

World Cup History

- Four appearances
- Best finish: Round of 16
- FIFA Rank: #31
- 2026 Group: I

The Norwegians return to the World Cup for the first time since 1998. Their best finishes came with Round of 16 runs in 1938 and 1998. This generation changes the expectations because Norway now has two of the biggest attacking names in European football.

Group Stage Matches

- Norway vs. Iraq: June 16, 6:00PM ET
- Norway vs. Senegal: June 22, 8:00PM ET
- Norway vs. France: June 26, 3:00PM ET

Major Storylines, Predictions

Norway has arguably the greatest goalscorer of all-time in Erling Haaland and playmaking mastermind Martin Ødegaard. Their game against Senegal may be one of the most important group-stage swing matches. If Norway can defend well enough behind its attack, this could be their best World Cup team in decades.

Soccer Analyst’s Prediction: Norway will likely be the most entertaining team to watch in this field, and if they can somehow reach the Round of 16, Erling Haaland could have a shot at setting the single-tournament goal record. They could win advance and win one Knockout Stage game, but anything past that seems highly improbable.

Key Players
